measure: HB 2198 (repeal of data center sales tax exemption)
summary: House voted 197-5 to repeal the exemption. The Senate passed repeal language in a separate tax code bill. Neither version reached the governor.

measure: HB 1834 (PUC regulation of commercial data centers)
summary: Would require the PUC to assign connection, transmission, network upgrade, reliability, and PJM emergency capacity costs to data centers. Referred to Senate Consumer Protection and Professional Licensure on March 31, 2026.
Would let municipalities pause consideration of data center applications for up to 180 days while revising land use ordinances. Bill number and vote to be confirmed.

DEP reviews data center permit applications only if the developer makes a legally binding commitment to the GRID Requirements. Revenue must update exemption guidelines so new applicants comply with GRID.

measure: Data center energy and water reporting
summary: A PennFuture tracker reports that annual energy and water reporting requirements were enacted through FY 2026-27 budget implementation. Bill and code section not yet confirmed.
Budget kept the data center sales and use tax exemption. The Joint Subcommittee on Tax Policy must study the exemption and report by mid-December 2026.
New tax of $0.011 per kWh on data center electricity, capped at $600 million a year with excess refunded pro rata. Expires June 30, 2028 absent extension.

measure: Large-load cost allocation (25 MW and above)
summary: Costs of increased generating capacity assigned to customers with 25 MW or more of demand. HB 284 directs two utilities to create voluntary demand flexibility programs for those customers.

measure: HB 153 / SB 94: siting and pre-vote disclosure (Va. Code 15.2-2209.5)
summary: Governs where the largest facilities can go and what developers must disclose before a local board votes.
DEQ may not issue air permits for data center generators applied for on or after July 1, 2026 unless they meet Tier IV or an equivalent standard.
Water reporting authority takes effect January 1, 2027. DEQ cooling water scarcity area regulations due July 1, 2027. Budget also requires data centers to limit water use for cooling.
First annual SCC report on aggregated data center electricity, water, and generator data.

measure: Data Center Accountability Framework and Executive Order 22
summary: Framework on local approval transparency, energy costs, and environmental standards. EO 22 implements core pieces and creates an AI Task Force.
Of 61 data center bills considered in 2026, 15 went to the governor and 46 carry over to 2027.

measure: Pause on new sales tax exemption requests
summary: Governor DeWine directed the Tax Credit Authority to pause consideration of new data center exemption requests while the Joint Data Center Committee studies data center growth.
PUCO-approved tariff requires new data centers to pay for at least 85% of the load they request. The Ohio Manufacturers' Association is challenging it at the Ohio Supreme Court.

measure: House bill extending the AEP tariff approach statewide
summary: Bipartisan bill (Reps. Thomas and Rader) modeled on the AEP tariff.

measure: Senate data center bill (rate class; NDAs; water; local impacts)
summary: Would create a PUCO data center rate class and address tax breaks, nondisclosure agreements, water use, and local government impacts.

Defines large load customers for tariff purposes, requires data centers to pay for the infrastructure and grid costs they create, and requires confidential reporting aggregated into an annual public report.

Single state review for projects of 25 MW or more; new Data Center Task Force and public dashboard. Agencies defer substantive review until local land use approvals are documented; state incentives require alignment with state principles; agencies may not enter NDAs with data center developers.
BGE, Pepco, and Delmarva large load tariffs are before the Public Service Commission.
14 of 24 jurisdictions have moratoriums or bans (Daily Record count). Harford County passed the first indefinite ban in June; Frederick County extended its pause to July 1, 2027.

measure: Repeal of 2020 sales and use tax exemption
summary: Governor Moore will seek repeal in the 2027 General Assembly session.

measure: Sales tax exemption repeal and pause bills
summary: The Senate passed a repeal bill on March 6. The session ended with the exemption intact. SB 436 (suspend new certificates) and HB 1012 (construction pause) were introduced.
Passed the House 159-5. Did not become law.

measure: PSC large-load rules and generation approval
summary: Customers of 100 MW or more must take service under custom contracts. In December 2025 the PSC approved nearly 10,000 MW of new generation, roughly 80% expected to serve data centers. Base rates frozen through 2028.
Lets large customers, including data centers, fund their own clean energy projects for bill credits, up to 3 GW through 2035.
Two PSC seats on the ballot, with data center regulation a key campaign issue.
